DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.claim: Qaḍā can mean completing a term or period, and completing the revelation sent to someone.
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.anchor: الثامن : قضى أتم قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r5.claim: Calling God the King and the True follows the Quran's exaltation: kingship conveys sovereignty, truth excludes false claimed gods, and the preceding passage displayed His power and servants' humility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r5.anchor: ذكر عظمة منزله تعالى ثم ذكر هاتين الصفتين وهي صفة الملك التي تضمنت القهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r6.claim: Do not hasten the Quran means wait until the one conveying revelation finishes; do not synchronize one's recitation with it, as also stated in a passage in al-Qiyama.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r6.anchor: أي تأن حتى يفرغ الملقي إليك الوحي ولا تساوق في قراءتك قراءته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r7.claim: Another reading of the command is not to deliver a still-general passage before its clarification comes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا تبلغ ما كان منه مجملا حتى يأتيك البيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r8.claim: One occasion report says a woman complained that her husband slapped her; after the Prophet initially said there would be retaliation, the ruling about men caring for women was revealed and this verse directed him to wait before judging from Quran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p386/r8.anchor: وقيل: سبب الآية أن امرأة شكت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r1.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r1.claim: Al-Mawardi says the command means not to ask before revelation: Meccans and the bishop of Najran requested answers within three days, revelation was delayed, and rumors arose that Muhammad had been defeated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r1.anchor: وقال الماوردي: معناه ولا تسأل قبل أن يأتيك الوحي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r2.claim: Abu Muslim allows the command to concern hastening one's private reading, recitation to others, interpreting its apparent sense, or teaching others what its apparent sense entails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r2.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم ولا تعجل بقراءته في نفسك أو في تأديته إلى غيرك أو في اعتقاد ظاهره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r3.claim: The revelation's completion or explanation may be what the Prophet must await; he and others should suspend judgment until possible specifications such as exceptions or conditions arrive, and the haste may have been ijtihad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r3.anchor: من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه أي تمامه أو بيانه احتمالات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r4.claim: The majority read يقضى passively with وحيه as its nominative subject; several readers instead say نقضي with the majestic plural and make وحيه accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يقضى إليك مبنيا للمفعول وحيه مرفوع به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r5.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r5.claim: Al-Aʿmash shares the first-person plural reading but leaves the yāʾ of نقضي quiescent, following a dialect that does not open it at a word ending after kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش كذلك إلا أنه سكن الياء من يقضي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r6.claim: Maqatil glosses the request for increased knowledge as asking for more Quran.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r7.claim: Other explanations take knowledge here as understanding or memorization.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r8.claim: The request expresses humility and gratitude for the subtle instruction and refined etiquette just taught; God commanded His Messenger to seek increase in nothing else as He did in knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p387/r8.anchor: وهذا القول متضمن للتواضع لله والشكر له عند ما علم من ترتيب التعلم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r4.claim: The Qur’an is the Prophet’s sole weapon against opponents; it guides him through hardship, reassures him, and answers their repeated challenges. The Prophet eagerly awaited revelation like a soldier waiting for supplies to face a large army.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r4.anchor: the sole weapon of the Prophet (sws) against the onslaughts of his rivals

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r5.claim: He should not demand the Qur’an before its appointed gradual revelation is complete, since God knows its timing and wisdom; he should pray for increased knowledge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r5.anchor: God fully knows the wisdom in the time span He has allocated for it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r6.speaker: Our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r6.claim: Exegetes say the Prophet hurried to acquire revelation while Gabriel recited it and was told to stop; Islahi accepts eagerness as natural.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p74/r6.anchor: Our exegetes have confined its meaning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r6.claim: Although eagerness to receive revelation is natural, Islahi rejects it as the reason the Prophet was stopped; the wider context explains the warning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r6.anchor: the whole matter will become evident

RAZI-FULL:v32p174/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p174/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p174/r7.claim: Razi presents God addressing the Prophet: his heart, tongue, and body belong to God; ask God for knowledge, worldly provision, or protection from harm.
RAZI-FULL:v32p174/r7.anchor: قلبك لي فلا تدخل فيه حب غيري ، ولسانك لي فلا نذكر به أحدا غيري

ELMALILI:20:105-115/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:105-115/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:105-115/r4.claim: He renders God as the true, exalted sovereign and preserves the prayer asking God to increase the Prophet’s knowledge.
ELMALILI:20:105-115/r4.anchor: sana vahyi tamam edilmeden evvel Kur’ân’ı acele etme ve de ki رَبِّ زِدْن۪ي عِلْماً “Rabbim artır beni ilimce”

QUSHAYRI:v2p274/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p274/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p274/r15.claim: God’s majesty means His glory, exaltation, praise, elevation, grandeur, and entitlement to attributes of majesty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p274/r15.anchor: وكبرياؤه : سناؤه وعلاه ومجده ورفعته وعظمته

FARRA:v2p192/r16.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p192/r16.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p192/r16.claim: The Prophet hurried to recite revelation before Gabriel had finished; he was told to wait until Gabriel completed it.
FARRA:v2p192/r16.anchor: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه جبريل بالوحي عجل بقراءته قبل أن يستتم جبريل تلاوته

FARRA:v2p192/r17.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p192/r17.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p192/r17.claim: Here forgetting means leaving what one had been commanded to do.

TABATABAI:20:99-114/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:99-114/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:99-114/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī questions the saying that one should wish the sun not to rise after a day without knowledge bringing one nearer to God: the Prophet would not curse himself over what he cannot control, and transmission by meaning may have distorted it.
TABATABAI:20:99-114/r1.anchor: والحديث لا يخلو من شيء وكيف يظن بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يدعو على نفسه في أمر ليس إليه، ولعل في الرواية تحريفا من جهة النقل بالمعنى

SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r1.claim: The general reading has يُقضى in the passive, with وحيه nominative as the deputy subject.
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r1.anchor: العامة على بناء " يقضى " للمفعول ورفع " وحيه " لقيامه مقام الفاعل.

SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r2.speaker: الجحدري وأبو حيوة والحسن وعبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r2.claim: Al-Jahdari, Abu Haywa, al-Hasan, and the reading of Abd Allah have نقضي in the active first-person plural, with وحيه as its object.
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r2.anchor: والجحدري وأبو حيوة والحسن وهي قراءة عبد الله " نقضي " بنون العظمة مبنيا للفاعل،

SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r3.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r3.claim: Al-A mash shares the active reading but makes the final radical vowelless, avoiding a movement judged heavy on a weak letter.
SAMIN-DURR:20:114/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش كذلك، إلا أنه سكن لام الفعل. استثقل الحركة وإن كانت خفيفة

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r8.claim: Do not hasten the Qur'an before its revelation has been made clear to you.
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r8.anchor: أي من قبل أن يبين لك بيانه، ويقرأ من قبل أن نقضي إليك وحيه

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r9.claim: The clause is read بالنون نقضي, or بالياء يقضي with God as subject; تقضي was not read.
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r9.anchor: ويجوز من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه، أي من قبل أن يقضي الله إليك وحيه

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r10.claim: The readings are يقضى and نقضي with yāʾ or nūn; تقضي is not read.

ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r1.claim: God is exalted as Ultimate Sovereign and Ultimate Truth.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r1.anchor: the Ultimate Sovereign, the Ultimate Truth

ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r2.claim: The Prophet is told not to hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is complete.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r2.anchor: and [knowing this,] do not approach the Qur'an in haste, [100] ere it has been revealed unto thee in full

ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r3.claim: The verse directs the Prophet to pray for increased knowledge.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114/r3.anchor: [always) say: "O my Sustainer, cause me to grow in knowledge!"

ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r1.claim: When al-haqq designates God, it means absolute, intrinsic truth that exists eternally and immutably beyond creation's changing phenomena.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r1.anchor: it signifies "the Truth" in the absolute, intrinsic sense, eternally and immutably existing beyond the ephemeral, changing phenomena of His creation

ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r2.claim: Al-malik denotes God's absolute sway over all existence and is rendered “Ultimate Sovereign.”
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n99/r2.anchor: God's attribute of al-malik, on the other hand, denotes His absolute sway over all that exists

ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n100/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n100/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n100/r1.claim: Asad gives the literal rendering “be not hasty with the Qur'an” and points to the following note for explanation.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n100/r1.anchor: Lit., "be not hasty with the Qur'an" (see next note)

ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r1.claim: Asad considers it very probable that this exhortation first addressed Muhammad, as most classical commentators say.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r1.anchor: it is very probable that - as most of the classical commentators point out - this exhortation was in the first instance addressed to the Prophet Muhammad

ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r2.claim: The exhortation also applies to every person who reads the Qur'an, at any time.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r2.anchor: there is no doubt that it applies to every person, at all times, who reads the Qur'an.

ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r3.claim: Because the Qur'an is one coordinated whole, readers should let its full message shape their understanding and avoid conclusions from isolated verses; Asad links this to 25:32 and 75:16-19.
ASAD-NOTES:20:114#n101/r3.anchor: all its component parts - phrases, sentences, verses and surahs - form one integral, coordinated whole

QIRAAT-ER:20:114:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:114:10#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:20:114:10#1/r1.claim: Dropping hamza gives qurān instead of qurʾān; the source describes this as phonological simplification without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:20:114:10#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Hamza dropped: qurʾān → qurān; simplification of the glottal stop without semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:20:114:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:114:14#1/r1.speaker: Imp|CE
QIRAAT-ER:20:114:14#1/r1.claim: The active first-person plural naqḍiya changes the passive “it is completed” to direct divine agency: God completes the revelation.
QIRAAT-ER:20:114:14#1/r1.anchor: Imp|CE, mutawatir: "Active voice, 1st person plural (We complete): transforms passive ""it is completed"" to active divine agency

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the completion of revelation as its clarification.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه ﴾ قال تبيانه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r1.claim: The opening glorifies God and the Qur’an’s promises, warnings, commands, and prohibitions, declaring God transcendent and the revelation directed toward perfecting conduct—leaving sin and doing good.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r1.anchor: استعظام له تعالى ولما صرف في القرآن من الوعد والوعيد والأوامر والنواهي وغير ذلك وتنزيه لذاته المتعالية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r2.claim: The wording also expresses wonder and calls the listener to turn toward God and glorify Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r2.anchor: وفيه تعجيب واستدعاء للاقبال عليه وعلى تعظيمه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r3.claim: God is the sovereign who commands and forbids, rightly feared for His threats and hoped in for His promises; Qur’anic injunctions are divine governance for the good of both worlds.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r3.anchor: وفي وصفه تعالى بقوله سبحانه ( الملك ( أي المتصرف بالأمر والنهي الحقيق بأن يرجى وعده ويخشى وعيده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib explains al-Ḥaqq as the one who brings a thing into existence according to wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r4.anchor: وفسره الراغب بموجدالشئ على ما تقتضيه الحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥaqq may modify God, meaning true in essence and attributes, or modify King, meaning God’s sovereignty is true and deserved; either reading signals the Qur’an’s unassailable truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r5.anchor: وجوز غير واحد كونه صفة للملك ومعناه خلاف الباطل أي الحق في ملكيته يستحقها سبحانه لذاته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r6.claim: The description of God and His revelation prepares for the prohibition of haste: only the wretched abandons the Qur’an’s guidance, so the listener must attend to and honor it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r6.anchor: وفيه تمهيد لوصل النهي عن العجلة به في قوله سبحانه ( ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى اليك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r7.claim: The prohibition means not to rush before Gabriel has completed conveying the revelation; honoring the Qur’an requires focused reception.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r7.anchor: أي يتم ﴿ وحيه ﴾ أي تبليغ جبريل عليه السلام إياه فان من حق الاقبال ذلك وكذلك من حق تعظيمه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r8.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṭībī connects the prohibition with the preceding glorification: after recognizing the Sender’s majesty and the revelation’s grandeur, one should preserve and understand the Book without haste.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r8.anchor: وذكر الطيبي أن هذة الجملة عطف على قوله تعالى ( فتعالى الله الملك الحق ) لما فيه من انشاء التعجب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r9.claim: The Prophet used to repeat each letter and word after Gabriel for fear Gabriel would depart before he memorized it; hurrying could distract him from hearing what came next, and 75:16 was also revealed about this.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r9.anchor: وكان ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) إذا القى عليه جبريل عليه السلام القرإن يتبعه عند تلفظ كل حرف وكل كلمة خوفا أن يصعد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r10.claim: God commands the Prophet inwardly to ask Him for an increase in knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p267#2/r10.anchor: وأمر ( صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ) باستفاضة العلم واستزادته منه سبحانه فقيل : ( وقل ( أي في نفسك ﴿ رب زدني علما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r1.claim: Rather than rushing, the Prophet should ask for more knowledge generally or for more Qur’anic knowledge, since each word and letter contains many secrets, symbols, and sciences; this is more beneficial.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r1.anchor: أي سل الله عز وجل بدل الأستعجال زيادة العلم مطلقا أو في القرإن فان تحت كل كلمة بل كل حرف منه اسرار أو رموز أو علوما جمة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r2.claim: One view treats the prohibition as an excursus inserted after the revelation passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r2.anchor: وقيل : وجملة ( ولا نعجل ) مستانفة ذكرت بعد الأنزال على سبيل الاستطراد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the verse forbids communicating an ambiguous revelation before its explanation: reciting and conveying it before clarification is valid and lawful.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن ذلك نهى عن تبليغ ما كان مجملا قبل أن يأتي بيانه وليس بذاك فان تبليغ المجمل وتلاوته قبل البيان مما لا ريب في صحته ومشروعيته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r4.claim: A still weaker proposal says the Prophet was forbidden to order the Qur’an written before its meanings were explained and settled with him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r4.anchor: ومثله ما قيل : إنه نهى عن الأمر بكتابته قبل أن تفسر له المعاني وتتقرر عنده عليه الصلاة والسلام بل هو دونه بكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that a woman complained her husband slapped her; the Prophet first prescribed retaliation, then the verse about men’s authority over women was revealed and he paused. Al-Ālūsī rejects this explanation of the prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r5.anchor: بناء على ما أخرج جماعة عن الحسن أن امرأة شكت إلى النبي ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) أن زوجها لطمها فقال لها : بينكما القصاص

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r6.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r6.claim: Al-Māwardī says Meccans and the Najrān bishop gave the Prophet three days to answer questions; when revelation was delayed and Jews spread rumors, he became distressed and hurried it. Al-Ālūsī finds this and the preceding proposal unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r6.anchor: وقال الماوردي : إنه نهى عن العجلة بطلب نزوله وذلك أن أهل مكة واسقف نجران قالوا : يا محمد اخبرنا عن كذا وقد ضربنا لك أجلا ثلاثة ايام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r7.speaker: عبد الله والجحدري والحسن وأبو حيوة وسلام ويعقوب والزعفراني وابن مقسم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r7.claim: These readers say نقضى with the first-person plural, fatḥa on its final yāʾ, and وحيه in the accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والجحدري والحسن وابو حيوة وسلام ويعقوب والزعفراني وابن مقسم ( نقضى ) بنون العظمة مفتوح الياء ( وحيه ) بالنصب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r8.speaker: الأعمش؛ صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads the same construction but with a quiescent final yāʾ; al-Lawāmiʿ attributes this to a dialect that does not open final yāʾ after a kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r8.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش كذلك إلا أنه سكن الياء من ( نقضى ) قال صاحب اللوامح : وذلك عن لغة من لا يرى فتح الياء بحال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r9.claim: The command to seek more knowledge demonstrates its virtue; some say the Prophet was commanded to seek increase in no other thing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r9.anchor: واستدل بالآية على فضل العلم حيث أمر ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) بطلب زيادته وذكر بعضهم أنه ما أمر عليه الصلاة والسلام بطلب الزيادة في شئ إلا العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة؛ رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet’s prayer: ‘O God, benefit me with what You taught me, teach me what benefits me, increase me in knowledge, and praise be to God in every state’; cited from al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah, without a grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p268/r10.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي : وابن ماجه عن أبي هريرة قال : كان رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) يقول : اللهم انفعنى بما علمتنى وعلمنى ما ينفعنى وزدنى علما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd used to pray for increased faith, understanding, certainty, and knowledge; Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd transmit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r1.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد عن ابن مسعود أنه كان يدعو اللهم زدنى إيمانا وفقها ويقينا وعلما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this further reflects knowledge’s great merit and prays for increased knowledge and the ability to act upon it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269/r2.anchor: وما هذا إلا لزيادة فضل العلم وفضله اظهر من أن يذكر نسأل الله تعالى أن يرزقنا الزيادة فيه ويوفقنا للعمل بما يقتضيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p289/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289/r3.speaker: some interpreters
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289/r3.claim: Some take the prayer for increased knowledge as an allusion to knowledge bestowed directly by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289/r3.anchor: وقيل : هذا إشارة إلى العلم اللدني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r6.claim: God is exalted above the heretics’ denial and the claims made by the polytheists.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r6.anchor: جل الله عن إلحاد الملحدين وعما يقوله المشركون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r7.claim: When Gabriel recited, the Prophet hurried to read along before he finished, fearing the recitation might escape him or be forgotten; God forbade this haste.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r7.anchor: كان إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالقرآن يبادر فيقرأ معه، قبل أن يفرغ جبريل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r8.claim: The Prophet is told not to recite until Gabriel has finished conveying the revelation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r8.anchor: من قبل أن يفرغ جبريل من الإبلاغ، نظيره قوله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r9.claim: The prohibition is compared with the instruction not to move one’s tongue hastily over revelation in 75:16.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r9.anchor: نظيره قوله تعالى: "لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به" (سورة القيامة: 16)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r10.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r10.claim: Yaʿqūb reads نقضي with an open nūn, kasra on ḍād, and fatḥa on yāʾ, and reads وحيه in the accusative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r10.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب: " نقضي " بالنون وفتحها وكسر الضاد، وفتح الياء: " وحيه " بالنصب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r11.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r11.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say this means not to read or dictate it to the Companions until its meanings become clear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: معناه لا تقرئه أصحابك، ولا تمله عليهم حتى يتبين لك معانيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.claim: The requested increase in knowledge concerns the Qur’an and its meanings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.anchor: وقل رب زدني علما} يعني بالقرآن ومعانيه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the prayer asks for knowledge beyond what the speaker has already been taught.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.claim: When reciting this verse, Ibn Masʿūd would pray for increased knowledge, faith, and certainty.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال: اللهم رب زدني علما وإيمانا ويقينا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r1.claim: God's essence and attributes transcend likeness to creatures; His speech differs from theirs as His essence differs from theirs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r1.anchor: في ذاته وصفاته عن مماثلة المخلوقين لا يماثل كلامه كلامهم كما لا تماثل ذاته ذاتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r2.claim: God's command and prohibition take effect, and He rightly inspires hope in His promise and fear of His threat.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r2.anchor: النافذ أمره ونهيه الحقيق بأن يرجى وعده ويخشى وعيده

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r3.claim: Al-ḥaqq may mean rightful in His dominion by virtue of His essence, or true in His essence and attributes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r3.anchor: في ملكوته يستحقه لذاته، أو الثابت في ذاته وصفاته

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r4.claim: The primary prohibition is against hastening to receive revelation from Gabriel or reciting along before he completes it; the mention of revelation follows an aside about its sending.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r4.anchor: نهي عن الاستعجال في تلقي الوحي من جبريل عليه السلام ومساوقته في القراءة حتى يتم وحيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r5.claim: Another view prohibits conveying material stated generally before its clarification arrived.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r5.anchor: وقيل نهي عن تبليغ ما كان مجملا قبل أن يأتي بيانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r6.claim: Instead of hastening, the Prophet asks God for more knowledge, since revelation will certainly reach him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r6.anchor: أي سل الله زيادة العلم بدل الاستعجال فإن ما أوحى إليك تناله لا محالة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r5.claim: The preceding verses reach the height of eloquence and wisdom, displaying complete knowledge, power, and justice; after exalting His book, God exalts Himself to teach servants His due.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r5.anchor: دالة على أن لقائلها تمام العلم والقدرة والعدل ف أحوال الدراين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r6.claim: God's transcendence exceeds what describers can fully express or intellects can encompass, and is untouched by the false descriptions of deniers and polytheists.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r6.anchor: بلغ الذي لا يبلغ الواصفون وصفه حق وصفه من العلو أمرا لاتحتمله العقول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r7.claim: God is the King whom nothing can overcome and the only true sovereign; His kingship is real and never passes away.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r7.anchor: الذي لا يعجزه شيء , فلا ملك في الحقيقة غيره { الحق } اي الثابت الملك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r8.claim: In context, the command not to turn away from the remembrance is followed by a warning not to rush ahead by reciting the Qur'an before its revelation is complete.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r8.anchor: فلا تعرض عنه , بل أقبل عليه لتكون من المتقين الذاكرين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r9.claim: Here hastening with the Qur'an specifically means hastening its recitation.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r10.claim: The prepositional phrase makes the prohibition cover all times before completion, while the passive construction focuses on revelation being completed rather than on a particular revealer.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r10.anchor: بنى للمجهول قوله : { يقضى } أي ينهى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r11.claim: God did not send the Qur'an all at once but in measured, successive revelation; the Prophet should listen attentively, then recite after it is complete.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r11.anchor: كما أنا لم نعجل بإنزاله عليك جملة , بل رتلناه لك ترتيلا , زنزلناه إليك تنزيلا مفصلا تفصيلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r12.claim: The Prophet asks his nurturing Lord to deepen his understanding of what has been revealed and to reveal further knowledge, including knowledge that draws people to follow him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r12.anchor: أي بتفهيم ما أنزلت إلي منه وإنزال غيره كما زدتني بإنزاله وتحفيظه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r13.claim: Careful reflection and listening benefit learning more than haste and aid retention; what is fully understood is best preserved.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r13.anchor: أن التاني في العلم بالتدبر وبإلقاء السمع أنفع من الاستعجال المتعب للبال المكدر للحال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet prayed for benefit from learned knowledge, useful knowledge, increase in knowledge, praise in every condition, and refuge from the state of the people of Hell; al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and al-Bazzar transmit it, with no grading stated here.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r14.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.claim: The Moses story displays God's patience with servants who forget covenants; after praising the Reminder, condemning those who turn away, and instructing the Prophet about it, the sūra turns to Adam to warn against forgetfulness and urge repentance, showing God's ancient practice of forbearance toward inherently deficient people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.anchor: أتبع ذلك سبحانه قصة آدم عليه السلام تحذيرا من الركون إلى ما يسبب النسيان

DURR-FULL:v5p601/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the Prophet strained to memorize each Quranic revelation, fearing Gabriel would depart before he learned it; the command eases that effort and is linked to 75:16.
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r6.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أنزل عليه جبريل بالقرآن أتعب نفسه في حفظه حتى يشق على نفسه

DURR-FULL:v5p601/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet should wait until God makes the revelation clear to him.
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} يقول: لا تعجل حتى نبينه لك

DURR-FULL:v5p601/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r8.claim: Al-Hasan reports that after a man struck his wife and she sought retaliation, the Prophet initially ordered reciprocal punishment; this revelation made him wait until 4:34 arrived.
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r8.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لطم رجل امرأته فجاءت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تطلب قصاصا فجعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بينهما القصاص فأنزل الله {ولا تعجل بالقرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p601/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r9.claim: Al-Hasan is reported reciting the phrase with the passive verb form يَقْضَى.
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r9.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قرأ {من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه}

DURR-FULL:v5p601/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r10.claim: Mujahid says not to recite the Quran to anyone before God has completed its revelation to the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v5p601/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن} قال: لا تمله على أحد حتى نتمه لك

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the completion of revelation as its clarification.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} قال: تبيانه

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r2.claim: The Prophet prayed that God make his existing knowledge beneficial, teach him what benefits him, and increase his knowledge, while he praised God in every condition.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: اللهم انفعني بما علمتني وعلمني ما ينفعني وزدني علما

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r3.claim: Ibn Masud used a prayer asking God to increase him in faith, understanding, certainty, and knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود: أنه كان يدعو: اللهم زدني إيمانا وفقها ويقينا وعلما

BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r7.claim: God is exalted above every rank because He is the necessary, effective cause, while everything else is a possible effect; there is no likeness between them.
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r7.anchor: وليست مرتبة شريفة إلا والحق تعالى في أعلى الدرجات منها وأرفعها وذلك لأنه مؤثر وواجب لذاته وكل ما سواه أثر وممكن

BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r8.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r8.claim: Al-Irshad glosses the declaration as magnifying God and His governance through commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats, and declaring Him unlike creation in every respect.
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r8.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" وهو استعظام له تعالى ولشؤونه التي يصرف عليها عباده من الأوامر والنواهي والوعد والوعيد

BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r9.claim: Al-Malik is the sovereign whose commands and prohibitions take effect and whose promise merits hope and threat merits fear.
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r9.anchor: {الملك} السلطان النافذ أمره ونهيه الحقيق بأن يرجى وعده ويخشى وعيده

BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r10.claim: Al-Haqq means that God is true in sovereignty and divinity and intrinsically deserving of kingship.
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r10.anchor: {الحق} في ملكوته وألوهيته الحقيقي بالملك لذاته

BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r11.claim: Here yuqda means that revelation is delivered, completed, or finished; the author compares the usage with the completion of a term in Yunus.
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r11.anchor: يؤدي ويتم ويفرغ قال تعالى : {لقضى إليهم أجلهم}

BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r12.claim: When Gabriel recited, the Prophet followed each letter and word to ensure reception and memorization; speaking over him could prevent hearing what followed.
BURSEVI:v5p331#3/r12.anchor: كان عليه السلام إذا ألقى إليه جبريل الوحي يتبعه عند تلفظ كل حرف وكل كلمة لكمال اغتنائه بالتلقي والحفظ فنهى عن ذلك

BURSEVI:v5p332/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p332/r1.claim: Do not hurry for fear the revelation will be forgotten or slip away before Gabriel finishes reciting and conveying it; read after he has delivered it fully.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r1.anchor: والمعنى لا تعجل بقراءة القرآن خوف النسيان والانفلات قبل أن يستتم جبريل قراءته ويفرغ من الإبلاغ والتلقين فإذا بلغ فاقرأه

BURSEVI:v5p332/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p332/r2.claim: The inward lesson is to be still, listen to the Quran, and contemplate its meanings and secrets so its lights illuminate and disclose its truths.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة إلى سكوته عند قراءة القرآن واستماعه والتدبر في معانيه وأسراره

BURSEVI:v5p332/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p332/r3.claim: The prayer seeks understanding of the Quran’s inexhaustible realities, illumination by its lights, and embodiment of its character.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r3.anchor: أي : فهما لإدراك حقائقه فإنها غير متناهية وتنورا بأنواره وتخلقا بخلقه

BURSEVI:v5p332/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p332/r4.claim: One view takes the requested knowledge as knowledge of the Quran, with each new revelation increasing the Prophet’s knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم علما بالقرآن فكان كلما نزل عليه شيء من القرآن ازداد به علما

BURSEVI:v5p332/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r5.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
BURSEVI:v5p332/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl reads the prayer as asking to know one’s own hidden evils, guile, and treachery so divine help can treat each with its remedy.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن الفضل علما بنفسي وما تضمره من الشرور والمكر والغدر لأقوم بمعونتك في مداواة كل شيء منها بدوائه

BURSEVI:v5p332/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v5p332/r6.claim: When Ibn Masud recited the verse, he prayed for increase in faith and certainty in God.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r6.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه إذا قرأها قال : اللهم زدني إيمانا ويقينا بك

BURSEVI:v5p332/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p332/r7.claim: Bursevi calls Ibn Masud’s reading the finest and most subtle interpretation because it directs faith and certainty to God alone, which is especially difficult.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r7.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه إذا قرأها قال : اللهم زدني إيمانا ويقينا بك وهو أجل التفاسير وأدقها

BURSEVI:v5p332/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r8.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p332/r8.claim: It is said that God commanded His Messenger to seek increase only in knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r8.anchor: قيل : ما أمر الله رسوله بطلب الزيادة في شيء إلا في العلم

BURSEVI:v5p332/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r9.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p332/r9.claim: Kashifi, citing Qushayri’s Latāʾif, contrasts Moses being directed to Khidr for added knowledge with Muhammad being taught this prayer without referral elsewhere, as a sign of his special instruction and adab.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r9.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در لطائف قشيري رحمه الله مذكوراست كه حضرت موسى عليه السلام زيادة علم طلبيد اورا حواله بخضر كردند

BURSEVI:v5p332/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p332/r10.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
BURSEVI:v5p332/r10.claim: Ibrahim al-Harawi reports Abu Yazid saying that ordinary people take knowledge from the dead, while they took knowledge from the Living who never dies.
BURSEVI:v5p332/r10.anchor: قال إبراهيم الهروي كنت بمجلس أبي يزيد البسطامي قدس سره فقال بعضهم إن فلانا أخذ العلم من فلان قال أبو يزيد المساكين أخذوا العلوم من الموتى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r3.claim: The praise is an interjection between the statement about Quranic revelation and the instruction not to hasten; it teaches thanks for the Quran’s means of reform, exhortation, and eloquent guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r3.anchor: وجملة فتعالى الله الملك الحق } معترضة بين جملة { وكذلك أنزلناه } وبين جملة { ولا تعجل بالقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r4.claim: The revelation and its reforming means flow from God’s exaltation and greatness as the true King, who governs His subjects with complete perfection and effective rule.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r4.anchor: والتفريع مؤذن بأن ذلك الإنزال والتصريف ووسائل الإصلاح كل ذلك ناشىء عن جميل آثار يشعر جميعها بعلوه وعظمته وأنه الملك الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r5.claim: Calling God the true King implies that other figures called kings possess imperfect sovereignty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r5.anchor: وفي وصفه بالحق إيماء إلى أن ملك غيره من المتسمين بالملوك لا يخلو من نقص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r6.speaker: الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r6.claim: A hadith depicts God saying, I am the King; where are the kings of the earth? It challenges anyone to find a rival to His sovereignty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( فيقول الله أنا الملك أين ملوك الأرض ) ، أي أحضروهم هل تجدون منهم من ينازع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r7.speaker: معاوية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr compares the hadith’s challenge to Muʿāwiya’s address to the people of Medina, asking where their scholars were.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r7.anchor: كقول الخليفة معاوية حين خطب في المدينة ( يا أهل المدينة أين علماؤكم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r8.claim: Pairing the name Allah with the title King shows that God deserves reverence in Himself: the comprehensive divine name signifies all perfections and exclusive, complete divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p315/r8.anchor: والجمع بين اسم الجلالة واسمه ( الملك ) إشارة إلى أن إعظامه وإجلاله مستحقان لذاته بالاسم الجامع لصفات الكمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r1.claim: حق means sovereignty without any trace of incapacity or submission to another; the description implies that other kingship is false.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r1.anchor: والحق : الذي ليس في ملكه شائبة عجز ولا خضوع لغيره ، وفيه تعريض بأن ملك غيره زائف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r2.claim: As the true King, God’s actions plainly follow wisdom; the Quran is the law of His kingdom and the perfect policy securing the welfare of its followers in both worlds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r2.anchor: وفي تفريع ذلك على إنزال القرآن إشارة أيضا إلى أن القرآن قانون ذلك الملك ، وأن ما جاء به هو السياسة الكاملة الضامنة صلاح أحوال متبعيه في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r3.claim: The instruction not to hasten follows the preceding praise of the Quran and its extensive means for reforming people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r3.anchor: وجملة { ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه } ناشئة على ما تقدم من التنويه بالقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r4.claim: The Prophet’s concern for his community’s reform and salvation may have led him, after hearing these verses, to desire more Quran and its speedy delivery; God told him to leave the timing to divine knowledge of their needs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r4.anchor: فلما كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حريصا على صلاح الأمة شديد الاهتمام بنجاتهم لا جرم خطرت بقلبه الشريف عقب سماع تلك الآيات رغبة أو طلبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r5.claim: The phrase means before the revelation decreed for you has been completed, that is, before the portion slated for sending has finished being revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r5.anchor: أي من قبل أن يتم وحي ما قضي وحيه إليك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r6.claim: The prohibition targets asking or inwardly yearning intensely for faster revelation, as if it were delayed; it does not forbid simply wishing for more Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r6.anchor: فالمنهي عنه هو سؤال التعجيل أو الرغبة الشديدة في النفس التي تشبه الاستبطاء لا مطلق مودة الازدياد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r7.claim: The Prophet said he wished Moses had been patient with al-Khiḍr so that God could tell them more of their story, an example of wanting further revelation without demanding haste.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r7.anchor: فقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في شأن قصة موسى مع الخضر عليهما السلام ( وددنا أن موسى صبر حتى يقص الله علينا من أمرهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes hastening with the Quran as reciting while Gabriel delivers it: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet read ahead before Gabriel finished from eagerness to memorize and fear of forgetting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r8.anchor: فعن ابن عباس : كان النبي يبادر جبريل فيقرأ قبل أن يفرغ جبريل حرصا على الحفظ وخشية من النسيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives the same explanation for the command not to move the tongue hastily in the Quran, as cited in Sahih al-Bukhari.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r9.anchor: وهذا كما قال ابن عباس في قوله تعالى : لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به } ( القيامة : 16 ) كما في ( صحيح البخاري )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r10.claim: Under either interpretation, completing the revelation means finishing the portion then in the process of descending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p316/r10.anchor: وعلى هذين التأويلين يكون المراد بقضاء وحيه إتمامه وانتهاؤه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r14.claim: This closes the preceding account of God's sovereignty at judgment, power, servants' lowliness, and kindness before a different discourse begins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r14.anchor: ختم للقول لأنه لما قدم صفة سلطانه يوم القيامة وعظم قدرته وذلة عبيده وحسن تلطفه بهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r15.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r15.claim: One explanation says Muhammad feared forgetting the start of the Qur'an and recited before Gabriel completed the revelation; the verse parallels 75:16.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p65#2/r15.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخاف وقت تكلم جبريل له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r1.claim: A group says the Prophet was told to have revelation written at once; this verse ordered him to wait until its meanings were explained and settled.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r1.anchor: وقالت فرقة سبب هذه الآية أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا أوحي إليه القرآن أمر بكتبه للحين فأمره الله تعالى في هذه الآية أن يتأنى حتى يفسر له المعاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r2.claim: Another account says a woman complained that her husband slapped her; after Muhammad prescribed retaliation, 4:34 was revealed, and this verse taught him to wait until a Qur'anic ruling was clear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r2.anchor: وقالت فرقة سبب الآية أن امرأة شكت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن زوجها لطمها فقال لها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بينكما القصاص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r3.claim: The majority read the verb in the third person: before its revelation is completed to you.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reads in the first-person plural: before We complete its revelation to you.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسعود «من قبل أن نقضي إليك وحيه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r5.claim: The rest of the verse is clear and expresses a desire for good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66/r5.anchor: وباقي الآية بين رغبة في خير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r1.claim: God is exalted above heretics' denial and polytheists' claims about His attributes; He is King, with everything in His hand, and the True. Ibn al-Jawzi links this wording to 10:32.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r1.anchor: أي جل عن إلحاد الملحدين وقول المشركين في صفاته الملك الذي بيده كل شيء الحق وقد ذكرناه في يونس 32

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r2.claim: Abu Salih reports from Ibn Abbas that Gabriel recited a passage and Muhammad began repeating its opening before Gabriel finished, fearing he would forget it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن جبريل كان يأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالسورة الآي فيتلوها عليه فلا يفرغ جبريل من آخرها حتى يتكلم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأولها مخافة أن ينساها فنزلت هذه الآية رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says a woman whose husband slapped her sought retaliation; Muhammad arranged retaliation, then paused when this verse came until 4:34 was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أن رجلا لطم امرأته فجاءت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تطلب القصاص فجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بينهما القصاص فنزلت هذه الآية فوقف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى نزل قوله تعالى الرجال قوامون على النساء النساء 34 قاله الحسن البصري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن ويعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud, al-Hasan, and Yaʿqub read the verb with first-person plural nūn, a kasra on ḍād, and fatḥa on yā; waḥyahu is accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والحسن ويعقوب نقضي بالنون وكسر الضاد وفتح الياء وحيه بنصب الياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r5.claim: On the first occasion report, the command means not to recite until Gabriel has finished reciting, out of fear of forgetting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r5.anchor: أحدها لا تعجل بتلاوته قبل ان يفرغ جبريل من تلاوته تخاف نسيانه هذا على القول الأول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r6.claim: Mujahid and Qatada understand the command as not teaching the companions until God makes the revelation clear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r6.anchor: والثاني لا تقرئ أصحابك حتى نبين لك معاينة قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r7.claim: Al-Mawardi gives a third sense: do not ask for the revelation to be sent before it comes to you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r7.anchor: والثالث لا تسأل إنزاله قبل أن يأتيك الوحي ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r8.claim: Muqatil interprets the request for increased knowledge as a request for more Qur'an.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r9.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r9.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi reports another interpretation: asking God for greater understanding.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r9.anchor: والثاني فهما والثالث حفظا ذكرهما الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r10.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r10.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi reports a third interpretation: asking God for better retention.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p325#2/r10.anchor: والثاني فهما والثالث حفظا ذكرهما الثعلبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r3.claim: God is exalted and holy as the true King; He, His promise and threat, His messengers, Paradise, Hell, and everything from Him are true.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r3.anchor: أي: تنزه وتقدس (3) الملك الحق، الذي هو حق، ووعده حق، ووعيده حق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r4.claim: God's justice means He does not punish anyone before warning them and sending messengers, leaving no excuse or doubt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r4.anchor: وعدله تعالى ألا يعذب أحدا قبل الإنذار وبعثة الرسل والإعذار إلى خلقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir connects this command to 75:16-19, where God tells the Prophet not to move his tongue hastily during revelation and promises its collection and explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r5.anchor: كقوله تعالى في سورة "لا أقسم بيوم القيامة" {لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به * إن علينا جمعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r6.claim: An authentic report from Ibn Abbas says revelation was difficult for the Prophet, who repeated Gabriel's words from concern to memorize them; God instructed him to listen until the angel finished, then recite.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r6.anchor: وثبت في الصحيح عن ابن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعالج من الوحي شدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r7.claim: The command is to listen until the angel completes the revelation, then recite; God will gather it in the Prophet's breast so he does not forget it, and explain it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r7.anchor: أي: بل أنصت، فإذا فرغ الملك من قراءته عليك فاقرأه بعده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r8.claim: The Prophet is instructed to ask God to increase him in knowledge.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r9.speaker: ابن عيينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r9.claim: Ibn Uyayna says the Prophet's knowledge continued increasing until God took his life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن عيينة، رحمه الله: ولم يزل صلى الله عليه وسلم في زيادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a report that revelation continued coming to the Messenger until it was at its greatest volume on the day he died.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r10.anchor: إن الله تابع الوحي على رسوله، حتى كان الوحي أكثر ما كان يوم توفي رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r11.claim: The Prophet prayed: O God, benefit me by what You taught me, teach me what benefits me, increase my knowledge, and praise belongs to God in every state; Ibn Majah transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p318#3/r11.anchor: وقال ابن ماجه: حدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة، حدثنا عبد الله بن نمير، عن موسى بن عبيدة، عن محمد بن ثابت، عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "اللهم انفعني بما علمتني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p319/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p319/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p319/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits Abu Hurayra's prayer report and calls it unusual by this route; al-Bazzar also transmits it and adds a plea for refuge from the condition of the people of Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p319/r1.anchor: وأخرجه الترمذي، عن أبي كريب، عن عبد الله بن نمير، به. وقال: غريب من هذا الوجه.

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r1.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r1.claim: Yaqub reads with first-person nūn and an active verb, attributing the act of completing the revelation to God and making revelation its object.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r1.anchor: قرأ يعقوب: من قبل أن نقضي بالنون وفتحها وكسر الضاد، وحيه منصوب الياء

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r2.claim: The other readers use a passive verb and make وحيه the nominative subject of the passive construction.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: يقضى بضم الياء الأولى، وفتح الضاد، وسكون الياء الثانية، وحيه يرفع على ما لم يسم فاعله

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r3.claim: تعالى is derived on the tafaʿala pattern from elevation and means that God is exalted.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r3.anchor: تعالى: تفاعل من العلو، وهو بمعنى علا

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r6.claim: Abu Muslim connects the prohibition to the earlier command: make the earth dust and do not hasten with the Quran.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r6.anchor: الواو في قوله: (ولا تعجل) عطف على قوله: (فقل ينسفها) أي: ينسفها ولا تعجل، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن، وجماعة
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r8.claim: The Prophet sometimes hurried to recite incoming revelation to retain it for fear of forgetting, so God forbade haste.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r8.anchor: كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ربما ينزل عليه الوحي، فيعجل بقراءته حرصا على أخذه؛ مخافة لنسيانه، فنهي عنه

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r9.claim: An alternative occasion says a man struck his wife, she sought retaliation before the Prophet, and after he ordered it this verse and then 4:34 were revealed.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r9.anchor: لطم رجل امرأته فطلبت القصاص عند رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، فأمر به، فنزل: ولا تعجل، ثم نزل: (الرجال قوامون على النساء)

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.claim: A further connection warns the Prophet not to hasten or forget as Adam did; one need not marvel at forgetfulness, since Adam, his father, also forgot.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.anchor: وقيل: لا تعجل ولا تنس هذا كما نسي آدم، فلا غرو إن نسيت فقد نسي آدم أبوك

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r11.claim: One may not convey revelation before its delivery is complete; the connected discourse supports Abu Ali’s view that general wording needs its specification and ambiguous wording its explanation before conveyance.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r11.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ولا تعجل) أنه لا يجوز إبلاغ شيء إلا بعد إتمام الإيتاء لاتصال الكلام بعضه ببعض

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r12.claim: One should not form a belief before revelation is complete, because the ending can change the meaning of what came first.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r12.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يجوز أن يبادر إلى اعتقاد حتى يتكامل الوحي؛ لأن آخر الكلام يغير فائدة أوله

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r13.claim: The prayer for increased knowledge demonstrates the merit of knowledge.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r13.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وقل رب زدني علما) على فضل العلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r1.claim: The exaltation magnifies God and the ordering of His servants through commands, prohibitions, promise, threat, reward, and punishment throughout His dominion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r1.anchor: استعظام له ولما يصرف عليه عباده من أوامره ونواهيه ووعده ووعيده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r2.claim: When Gabriel recites revelation, the Prophet should wait until he hears and understands it, then retain it rather than racing Gabriel in recitation; alternatively, he should not convey a general passage before its clarification arrives.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r2.anchor: فتأن عليك ريثما يسمعك ويفهمك . ثم أقبل عليه بالتحفظ بعد ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r3.claim: A reading has حتى تقضى إليك وحيه.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r4.claim: Asking for more knowledge expresses humility and gratitude for the instruction in proper learning, and asks for continuing increase because everything contains divine wisdom and knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r4.anchor: { رب زدني علما } متضمن للتواضع لله تعالى والشكر له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r5.claim: It is said that God commanded His Messenger to seek increase in nothing except knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p90#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : ما أمر الله رسوله بطلب الزيادة في شيء إلا في العلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is told not to ask for revelation before its appointed completion reaches him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r4.anchor: لا تسأل إنزاله قبل أن يقضى , أي يأتيك وحيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r5.speaker: عطية
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r5.claim: The instruction means not to convey the Quran to people before its explanation has come.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r5.anchor: لا تلقه إلى الناس قبل أن يأتيك بيان تأويله , قاله عطية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r6.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says Muhammad hurried recitation before Gabriel finished conveying revelation because he feared forgetting it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r6.anchor: لا تعجل بتلاوته قبل أن يفرغ جبريل من إبلاغه , لأنه كان يعجل بتلاوته قبل أن يفرغ جبريل من إبلاغه خوف نسيانه , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r7.claim: One interpretation asks for more religious instruction; knowledge needed by the Prophet or community cannot be withheld until he seeks it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r7.anchor: زدني أدبا في دينك , لأن ما يحتاج إليه من علم دينه لنفسه أو لأمته لا يجوز أن يؤخره الله عنده حتى يلتمسه منه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, it asks for more patience in obedience and fighting enemies, since knowledge makes patience easier.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r8.anchor: زدني صبرا على طاعتك وجهاد أعدائك , لأن الصبر يسهل بوجود العلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r9.claim: Another interpretation asks for knowledge of prophetic stories and the stations of God's friends.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r9.anchor: زدني علما بقصص أنبيائك ومنازل أوليائك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation asks for knowledge of the community's condition and what will happen to it after the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r10.anchor: زدني علما بحال أمتي وما تكون عليه من بعدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r11.claim: A fifth explanation: as more Quran is revealed to him, the Prophet's knowledge of it increases.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p428#2/r11.anchor: الخامس : معناه : { وقل رب زدني علما } لأنه كلما ازداد من نزول القرآن عليه

MUJAHID:v1p403#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p403#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p403#3/r1.claim: The Prophet should not recite the Quran to anyone before God has explained it to him.
MUJAHID:v1p403#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه ﴾ يقول لا تتله على أحد

MUQATIL:20:114/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:114/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:114/r1.claim: God's exaltation means that He is above; He is true King because everything else and other gods are false.

MUQATIL:20:114/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:114/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:114/r2.claim: Gabriel had not finished the revelation before the Prophet began repeating its opening; God tells him to wait until Gabriel completes it.
MUQATIL:20:114/r2.anchor: لم يفرغ جبريل، عليه السلام، من آخر الكلام، حتى يتكلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، بأوله

MUQATIL:20:114/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:114/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:114/r3.claim: Muqatil says the request to increase in knowledge means to increase in Quran.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r1.claim: God is exalted above conjectures, limits of human understanding, likeness to people, and resemblance to bodies.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r1.anchor: ارتفع عن فنون الظنون وأوهام الأفهام وتنزه عن مضاهاة الأنام ومشابهة الاجسام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r2.claim: He is the King on whom kings themselves depend.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r3.claim: “The True” means that God is truly worthy of divinity.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r4.claim: After mentioning the Quran and its revelation, the passage briefly digresses to instruct the Prophet about receiving it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r4.anchor: ولما ذكر القرآن وانزاله قال استطرادا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r5.claim: When Gabriel teaches the revelation, the Prophet should wait until he has heard and understood it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r6.claim: Here, not rushing with the Quran means not rushing to recite it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r7.claim: The Prophet is to wait until Gabriel finishes delivering the revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r7.anchor: من قبل أن يفرغ جبريل من الابلاغ

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r8.claim: He asks for increased knowledge of the Quran and its meanings.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r9.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r9.claim: A reported maxim says God commanded His Messenger to seek increase in nothing except knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#3/r9.anchor: قيل ما أمر الله رسوله بطلب الزيادة في شيء إلا في العلم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r10.claim: After recalling God's favors and revelation of the Qurʾān, the verse declares Him exalted above offspring and equals.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r10.anchor: لما عرف العباد عظيم نعمه، وإنزال القرآن نزه نفسه عن الأولاد والأنداد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r11.claim: The true King means the One who possesses the truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r11.anchor: أي جل الله الملك الحق أي ذو الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r12.claim: God instructs the Prophet in how to receive the Qurʾān.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet recited before Gabriel finished revealing, eager to memorize and fearing he would forget; God forbade it, as at 75:16.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان عليه السلام يبادر جبريل فيقرأ قبل أن يفرغ جبريل من الوحي حرصا على الحفظ

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r14.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r14.claim: Through Ibn Abī Najīḥ, Mujāhid explains the command as do not recite it before understanding it clearly.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r14.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد: قال: لا تتله قبل أن تتبينه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r15.claim: Another interpretation is do not ask for revelation before it comes to you.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r15.anchor: وقيل: «ولا تعجل» أي لا تسل إنزاله «من قبل أن يقضى» إليك أي يأتيك «وحيه».

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r16.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r16.claim: Another interpretation is do not give the Qurʾān to people before its explanation reaches you.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r16.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا تلقه إلى الناس قبل أن يأتيك بيان تأويله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r17.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r17.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the passage was revealed about a man who slapped his wife; after the Prophet granted her retaliation, 4:34 was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r17.anchor: وقال الحسن: نزلت في رجل لطم وجه امرأته، فجاءت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تطلب القصاص،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r18.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r18.claim: In al-Ḥasan's account, increased knowledge means understanding, since God corrected the Prophet's ruling on retaliation.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r18.anchor: ولهذا قال: «وقل رب زدني علما» أي فهما لأنه عليه السلام حكم بالقصاص وأبى الله ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r19.claim: The prayer asks God to increase the Prophet's understanding.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r19.anchor: «وقل رب زدني علما» أي فهما لأنه عليه السلام حكم بالقصاص

QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r20.speaker: ابن مسعود وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r20.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and others read من قبل أن نقضي with nūn, a kasra on ḍād, and وحيه in the accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:113-114/r20.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وغيره «من قبل أن نقضي» بالنون وكسر الضاد «وحيه» بالنصب.

QASHANI:20:111-115/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:111-115/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:111-115/r5.claim: God's exaltation is beyond estimation; as true King He governs all by will and power in justice, giving each its due according to wisdom.
QASHANI:20:111-115/r5.anchor: تناهى في العلو والعظمة بحيث لا يقدر قدره ولا يغدر أمره في ملكه

QASHANI:20:111-115/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:111-115/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:111-115/r6.claim: Moses must not rush, from longing for direct knowledge at the station of union, before its arrival is settled; knowledge descends according to the stages of receptivity.
QASHANI:20:111-115/r6.anchor: عند هيجان الشوق لغاية الذوق بتلقي العلم اللدني عن مكمن الجمع { من قبل } أن يحكم بوروده

QASHANI:20:111-115/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:111-115/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:111-115/r7.claim: Seeking knowledge has no end: pursue increase through purification, spiritual ascent, and adornment, since readiness rather than premature asking opens each higher and subtler knowledge.
QASHANI:20:111-115/r7.anchor: ولا تفتر عن الطلب والاستفاضة فإنه غير متناه، واطلب الزيادة فيه بزيادة التصفية والترقي

RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r11.claim: After magnifying the Qurʾān, God magnifies Himself; He is called the true King because His sovereignty neither vanishes nor changes, is not received from another, and belongs to no one more rightfully.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r11.anchor: فقال : { فتعالى الله الملك الحق } تنبيها على ما يلزم خلقه من تعظيمه

RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r12.claim: Taʿālā is a form of tafāʿala from height; divine height, greatness, and lordship share the sense of attributes of majesty beyond imagination and intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r12.anchor: وتعالى تفاعل من العلو وقد ثبت أن علوه وعظمته وربوبيته بمعنى واحد

RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r13.claim: God is transcendent above benefit and harm: He sent the Qurʾān to guide people, not to gain from obedience or suffer from disobedience; obedience occurs by His enabling and sins by His justice, each person being facilitated toward what he was created for.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105/r13.anchor: وهو منزه عن المنافع والمضار فهو تعالى إنما أنزل القرآن ليحترزوا عما لا ينبغي

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r1.claim: Abū Muslim says the discourse from the question about the mountains (20:105) ends here, and do not hasten with the Qurʾān begins a new address.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : إن من قوله : { ويسئلونك عن الجبال }

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r2.claim: A reported context says the Prophet feared missing part of the revelation and recited along with the angel; he was told to listen until the angel finished, then recite, since God would preserve him from error and forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r2.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام كان يخاف من أن يفوته منه شيء فيقرأ مع الملك فأمره بأن يسكت حال قراءة الملك

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r3.claim: One possible meaning is that the Prophet should not hurry to recite the Qurʾān inwardly to himself.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد لا تعجل بقراءته في نفسك

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r4.claim: Another possible meaning is that he should not hurry to deliver the Qurʾān to someone else.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن لا تعجل في تأديته إلى غيرك

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r5.claim: A third possible meaning is that he should not rush to settle on its apparent meaning.

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r6.claim: A fourth possible meaning is that he should not explain to others what its apparent meaning entails before the revelation is complete.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل في تعريف الغير ما يقتضيه ظاهره

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r7.claim: Before the revelation is completed can refer either to completion of its text or to clarification of its meaning, both of which require revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r7.anchor: تمامه ، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد من قبل أن يقضى إليك بيانه

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r8.claim: The precise rule is to restrain oneself and others until the text or its explanation is complete, since an utterance may still be qualified by an exception, condition, or other specification.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r8.anchor: يجب التوقف في معنى الكلام ما لم يأت عليه الفراغ لما يجوز أن يحصل عقيبه من استثناء أو شرط

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r9.claim: Muqātil and al-Suddī, with a transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ, say the Prophet rapidly repeated Gabriel’s recitation from fear of forgetting; he was told to wait until it ended, receive it calmly, and trust God to increase his understanding and knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r9.anchor: وهذا قول مقاتل والسدي ورواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda interpret the command as forbidding recitation to the Companions before the meanings had been revealed and explained.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r10.anchor: فتقرأه على أصحابك قبل أن يوحى إليك بيان معانيه وهذا قول مجاهد وقتادة

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r11.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports that Meccans and the bishop of Najrān demanded answers within three days; delayed revelation fueled a claim that the Jews had defeated Muḥammad, so this reading forbids hastening revelation’s descent through its stages from the Preserved Tablet to him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r11.anchor: قال الضحاك : إن أهل مكة وأسقف نجران قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan transmits an account in which a woman said her husband slapped her face; the Prophet ordered retaliation, then withheld it when this verse was revealed until 4:34 came down.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r12.anchor: روى الحسن أن امرأة أتت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī calls the account from al-Ḥasan remote and says the detailed explanation given first is the one to rely on.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r13.anchor: وهذا بعيد والاعتماد على التفصيل الأول

RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r14.claim: The command means that the Prophet should turn to God for increased knowledge, which comes through completion of the Qurʾān or clarification of what was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p105#2/r14.anchor: أمره بالفزع إلى الله سبحانه في زيادة العلم التي تظهر بتمام القرآن أو بيان ما نزل عليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p106/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106/r1.claim: Asked how hastening could be forbidden if done by revelation, al-Rāzī answers that the Prophet may have acted by personal reasoning, though refraining would have been preferable.
