RAZI-FULL:v22p106/r1.anchor: لعله فعله بالاجتهاد ، وكان الأولى تركه

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.claim: The Prophet’s excessive zeal in religious effort is juxtaposed with Adam’s negligence: humans may err through either excess or shortfall.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.anchor: فلما وصفه بالإفراط وصف آدم بالتفريط في ذلك فإنه تساهل في ذلك ولم يتحفظ

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.claim: The Prophet may have worried that the prohibition implied wrongdoing; the story reassures him that his haste sprang from devotion and care for revelation, unlike Adam’s lapse through neglect.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.anchor: فقيل له : إن كنت فعلت ما نهيت عنه فإنما فعلته حرصا منك على العبادة

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r1.claim: Al-malik intensifies mālik; true kingship is the power to create and to do so uniquely.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r1.anchor: و { الملك } : مبالغة من المالك ، وحقيقة الملك القدرة على الإيجاد ، والانفراد بذلك

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r2.claim: Al-ḥaqq describing God means the existent; the saying that the evil eye is true means it exists.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r2.anchor: و { الحق } : في وصفه - سبحانه - بمعنى الموجود ، ومنه قوله عليه السلام : ( العين حق )

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r3.claim: Al-ḥaqq can also mean the possessor of the right.

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r4.claim: Al-ḥaqq can also mean the one who establishes the right; Qushayri says all these senses are sound.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r4.anchor: ويكون بمعنى محق الحق . . . كل ذلك صحيح

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r5.claim: Muhammad hurried to receive the recitation from Gabriel for fear of forgetting, so God ordered him to receive it steadily and assured him that God would preserve it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r5.anchor: كان يتعجل بالتلقف من جبريل مخافة النسيان ، فأمره بالتثبت في التلقين ، وأمنه من طوارق النسيان

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r6.claim: The verse advises caution in judging by outward evidence before referring it to foundational principles.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r6.anchor: الآية تشير إلى طرف من الاحتياط في القضاء بالظواهر قبل عرضها على الأصول

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r7.claim: If investigation finds no specific proof, apply the wording's general import; this opposes the people who suspend judgment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r7.anchor: ثم إن لم يوجد ما يوجب بالتحقيق أجراه على مقتضى العموم بحق اللفظ ، بخلاف قول أهل التوقف

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r8.claim: More broadly, the instruction calls for deliberation, patience, and care in all matters.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r8.anchor: فالآية تشير إلى التثبت في الأمور وضرورة التمكث واللبث قصدا للاحتياط

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r9.claim: Even the most learned human, whom God taught what he did not know, is told to ask for more knowledge; God's subtle knowledge for His friends has no limit.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r9.anchor: ومن شهد له الحق بخصائص العلم حين قال : { وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم } [ النساء : 113 ] يقال له : { وقل رب زدنى علما }

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r10.claim: Muhammad is directed to seek added knowledge from God Himself, unlike Moses, whom God directed to learn from al-Khiḍr and who was told he could not endure his company before they parted.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r10.anchor: وموسى عليه السلام أحاله على الخضر حتى قال له : { هل أتبعك على أن تعلمن مما علمت رشدا }

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r11.claim: The command teaches that the servant's noblest quality is neediness expressed through supplication, rather than standing in a posture of self-assertion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r11.anchor: أشرف خصال العبد الوقوف في محل الافتقار ، والاتصاف بنعت الدعاء دون الوقوف في معرض الدعوى

STUDYQURAN:20:114/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r1.claim: One explanation is that the Prophet feared forgetting revelation and quickly repeated Gabriel's words while they were being revealed.
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r1.anchor: This verse refers to the Prophet’s fear of forgetting the verses of revelation, which led him to repeat quickly what was being revealed to him by the Archangel Gabriel

STUDYQURAN:20:114/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r2.claim: Alternatively, the verse admonishes the Prophet not to seek revelation before its proper time.
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r2.anchor: Alternatively, it could be an admonishment to the Prophet not to seek to receive the revelation before its appropriate time

STUDYQURAN:20:114/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r3.claim: Muslims commonly use the plea for increased knowledge, including students beginning their studies.
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r3.anchor: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge! is commonly invoked by Muslims at various times, such as when they are students beginning their studies

STUDYQURAN:20:114/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to pray that God not bless a day on which he gains no knowledge that brings him nearer to God.
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r4.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said, “If a day comes upon me in which I do not increase in a knowledge that draws me nearer to God

STUDYQURAN:20:114/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r5.claim: Since the Prophet is told to ask for more knowledge, all Muslims should do so a fortiori.
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r5.anchor: Thus, if the Prophet is told to pray for increase in knowledge, then, a fortiori, all Muslims are expected to do the same

STUDYQURAN:20:114/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r6.speaker: Ibn ʿArabī
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r6.claim: Ibn ʿArabī says the supplication is presented to the community so they too will seek increase from God; if exclusive to the Prophet, that would have been made clear.
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r6.anchor: Hence, Ibn ʿArabī says, “God did not say to His Prophet, Say, ‘My Lord! Increase me in knowledge!’

STUDYQURAN:20:114/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r7.claim: Sufis particularly use this supplication, though pious Muslims generally use it as well.
STUDYQURAN:20:114/r7.anchor: This supplication has often been a prayer of the Sufis in particular, although it is used by pious Muslims in general

TAB-FULL:v16p180/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r1.claim: God, alone worthy of worship, is exalted above creation; His sovereignty overpowers every king and tyrant, and He is true beyond the polytheists' descriptions.
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} [طه: 114] قال

TAB-FULL:v16p180/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r2.claim: The Prophet must not recite or dictate the Qur'an before its revelation and explanation are complete.
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r2.anchor: ولا تعجل يا محمد بالقرآن، فتقرئه أصحابك، أو تقرأه عليهم، من قبل أن يوحى إليك بيان معانيه

TAB-FULL:v16p180/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r3.claim: The admonition concerned dictating revealed text to a scribe before God clarified its meanings; he must wait to recite or dictate until then.
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r3.anchor: فعوتب على إكتابه وإملائه ما كان الله ينزله عليه من كتابه من كان يكتبه ذلك، من قبل أن يبين له معانيه

TAB-FULL:v16p180/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r4.claim: Mujāhid says not to recite the Qur'an to anyone until God explains it.
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} [طه: 114] قال: لا تتله على أحد حتى نبينه لك

TAB-FULL:v16p180/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says not to recite it to anyone until God completes it for the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: يقول: لا تتله على أحد حتى نتمه لك

TAB-FULL:v16p180/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet must not hasten until God explains the Qur'an to him.
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} [طه: 114] يعني: لا تعجل حتى نبينه لك

TAB-FULL:v16p180/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses the point as waiting for the Qur'an's explanation.
TAB-FULL:v16p180/r7.anchor: عن قتادة {من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} [طه: 114] من قبل أن يبين لك بيانه

SULAMI:v1p449#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#5/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p449#5/r1.claim: Some say the request means: make me knowledgeable of You and ignorant of everything besides You; that is true increase in knowledge.

SULAMI:v1p449#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#5/r2.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p449#5/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl reads the request as increased knowledge of one's own hidden evils, schemes, and excuses, so one can treat them with God's help.
SULAMI:v1p449#5/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل : ﴿ رب زدني علما ﴾ بنفسي

TABATABAI:20:113-114/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r2.claim: The glorification best follows the resurrection and judgment discussion: God’s absolute kingship includes guiding people by messengers and books, raising them, and judging their deeds.
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r2.anchor: وهذا هو الأنسب نظرا إلى انسلاك الجميع في سلك واحد وهو أنه تعالى ملك يتصرف في ملكه بهداية الناس

TABATABAI:20:113-114/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r3.claim: It may instead close the entire preceding account of Moses and its consequences with glorification and awe.
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r3.anchor: ويمكن أن يتفرع على جميع ما تقدم من قصة موسى وما فرع عليها إلى هنا ويكون بمنزلة ختم ذلك بالتسبيح والاستعظام

TABATABAI:20:113-114/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r4.claim: The context concerns receiving Quranic revelation: the Prophet is told not to rush his recitation before the angel has completed the revelation.
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r4.anchor: السياق يشهد بأن في الكلام تعرضا لتلقي النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وحي القرآن

TABATABAI:20:113-114/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r5.claim: The verse pairs the command not to hasten with the supplication for more knowledge, placing the Prophet’s continuing learning beside his recitation.
TABATABAI:20:113-114/r5.anchor: وحيه وقل رب زدني علما } السياق يشهد بأن في الكلام

TABATABAI:20:114/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:114/r1.claim: The command parallels the instruction not to move the tongue hastily; the Quranic passage says God gathers and recites it, then tells the Prophet to follow the recitation.
TABATABAI:20:114/r1.anchor: لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه

TABATABAI:20:114/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:114/r2.claim: The verse supports reports of a single, complete descent of the Quran in addition to its gradual descent: otherwise the Prophet could not hurry to recite what had not yet been revealed.
TABATABAI:20:114/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية مما يؤيد ما ورد من الروايات أن للقرآن نزولا دفعة واحدة غير نزوله نجوما

TABATABAI:20:114/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:114/r3.claim: One view says not to recite or dictate Quran to companions before its meanings become clear; the author finds no support for this in the wording.
TABATABAI:20:114/r3.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن لفظ الآية لا تعلق له بهذا المعنى

TABATABAI:20:114/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:114/r4.claim: Another view takes the verse as forbidding a request for revelation before God completes it; the author likewise finds this reading incompatible with the wording.
TABATABAI:20:114/r4.anchor: وهو كسابقه غير منطبق على لفظ الآية

TABATABAI:20:114/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114/r11.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
TABATABAI:20:114/r11.claim: In al-Kafi, Abu Qurra claims God granted vision to Muhammad and speech to Moses; al-Rida argues Muhammad conveyed that God is unseen, incomprehensible, and unlike creation, so reports contradicting Quran and Muslim consensus are rejected.
TABATABAI:20:114/r11.anchor: فقال أبو الحسن عليه السلام فمن المبلغ عن الله إلى الثقلين من الجن والإنس { لا تدركه الأبصار }

TABATABAI:20:114#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r1.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r1.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi says the Prophet would hasten to recite revelation before an ayah finished descending; the command told him to wait until its recitation was complete and ask for more knowledge.
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r1.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولا تعجل بالقرآن } الآية، قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:20:114#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r2.speaker: السدي
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi’s version says the Prophet hurried for fear of forgetting; al-Tabataba'i rejects this because forgetting revelation conflicts with prophetic infallibility.
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي إلا أن فيه أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يفعل ذلك خوفا من النسيان

TABATABAI:20:114#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports that after a husband struck his wife and the Prophet ordered retaliation, this verse was revealed before 4:34; the author says neither verse fits the event.
TABATABAI:20:114#2/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال لطم رجل امرأته فجلاءت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم تطلب قصاصا

TABRISI:20:114-115/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:114-115/r2.claim: God’s attributes transcend created attributes: creatures depend on Him, have limited knowledge and power, and may forget, while He is eternally knowing and powerful.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r2.anchor: ارتفعت صفاته عن صفات المخلوقين فلا يشبهه أحد من صفاته لأنه أقدر من كل قادر وأعلم من كل عالم

TABRISI:20:114-115/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:114-115/r3.claim: God owns this world and the next, and truly deserves kingship; every other king owns only some things and eventually loses his kingdom.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r3.anchor: والملك الذي يملك الدنيا والآخرة والحق الذي يحق له الملك وكل ملك سواه يملك بعض الأشياء ويبيد ملكه

TABRISI:20:114-115/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، الجبائي
TABRISI:20:114-115/r4.claim: Do not recite along with Gabriel for fear of forgetting; understand the revelation until he finishes, then recite, as in the command against moving the tongue hastily.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r4.anchor: وهذا كقوله لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به [القيامة: 16] عن ابن عباس والحسن والجبائي

TABRISI:20:114-115/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r5.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، عطية، أبو مسلم
TABRISI:20:114-115/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that Muhammad should not recite or dictate the Qur’an to his companions before its meanings become clear to him.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r5.anchor: ولا تقرأه لأصحابك ولا تمله عليهم حتى يتبين لك معانيه عن مجاهد وقتادة وعطية وأبي مسلم

TABRISI:20:114-115/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:114-115/r6.claim: Do not ask for the Qur’an to be sent down before its revelation arrives; God sends it when circumstances make it appropriate.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r6.anchor: وثالثها أن معناه ولا تسأل إنزال القرآن قبل أن يأتيك وحيه

TABRISI:20:114-115/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:114-115/r7.claim: The Prophet is told to ask God for knowledge beyond what he already has.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r7.anchor: أي استزد من الله سبحانه علما إلى علمك

TABRISI:20:114-115/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r8.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:20:114-115/r8.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet prayed that God not bless a day’s sunrise if he had gained no knowledge that brought him nearer to God.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r8.anchor: روت عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " إذا أتى علي يوم لا أزدد فيه علما يقربني إلى الله فلا بارك الله لي

TABRISI:20:114-115/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:114-115/r9.claim: One explanation is a request for knowledge of the prophets’ stories and the stations of God’s friends.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه زدني علما بقصص أنبيائك ومنازل أوليائك

TABRISI:20:114-115/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r10.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:20:114-115/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the request as asking for more Qur’an, since each additional revelation increased the Prophet’s knowledge.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r10.anchor: وقيل: زدني قرآنا لأنه كلما أزداد من نزول القرآن عليه ازداد علما عن الكلبي

TABRISI:20:115/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:115/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:115/r3.claim: The verses connect the command not to hurry with trust in God to preserve the Qur’an, since Adam forgot what had been entrusted to him.
TABRISI:20:115/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنه إتصل بقوله { ولا تعجل بالقرآن } أي لا تعجل خوف النسيان للفظه

THALABI:v6p261/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p261/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p261/r12.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the nūn and both yāʾs with fatḥa; the other readers use ḍamma on the first and final yāʾ and sukūn on the middle one.
THALABI:v6p261/r12.anchor: قرأ يعقوب بفتح النون والياءين، وقرأ الآخرون: بضم الياء الأولى والأخرى وسكون الوسطى

THALABI:v6p261/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p261/r13.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
THALABI:v6p261/r13.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say not to recite or dictate the verses to companions before their meanings become clear; al-ʿAwfī transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbās.
THALABI:v6p261/r13.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: لا تقرئه أصحابك ولا تمله عليهم حتى يتبين لك معانيه

THALABI:v6p261/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p261/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p261/r14.claim: Other reports from Ibn ʿAbbās say the Prophet repeated the Qurʾān along with Gabriel before Gabriel finished, eager to retain it and fearing it would slip away; God told him to wait until the recitation was complete.
THALABI:v6p261/r14.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل جبرائيل بالوحي يقرأه مع جبرائيل

THALABI:v6p261/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p261/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p261/r15.claim: The prayer asks for greater understanding of the Qurʾān; another view takes it as a request for memorization.
THALABI:v6p261/r15.anchor: وقيل: حفظا ونظيرها قوله لا تحرك به لسانك

THALABI:v6p261/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p261/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p261/r16.claim: The instruction is compared with the parallel command not to move the tongue hastily while reciting.
THALABI:v6p261/r16.anchor: ونظيرها قوله لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to recite before revelation to him is complete.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r1.anchor: لا تعجل بتلاوته قبل أن يفرغ من وحيه إليك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r2.claim: The Prophet used to hurry to recite before Gabriel finished, fearing he might forget.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283/r2.anchor: وكان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وعلى آله – يبادر بقراءته قبل أن يتمم جبريل، خوفا من النسيان.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r1.claim: God is exalted above the heretics' denial and is free of the attributes the polytheists ascribe to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r1.anchor: جل عن إلحاد الملحدين، ونزه عما يقول المشركون في صفته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r2.claim: Alternatively, God deserves incomparable praise: He is more powerful and knowing than any other, while every other possessor of power depends on Him and He depends on none.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r2.anchor: أقدر من كل قادر، وأعلم من كل عالم، وقادر سواه محتاج إليه وهو غني عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the King is the one in whose hand lie reward and punishment; the author explains that He owns them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد الذي بيده الثواب والعقاب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r4.claim: Al-Ḥaqq here means the possessor of truth or right; the author says he discussed this earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r4.anchor: {الحق} معناه: ذو الحق، وقد مر وتقدم الكلام فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r5.claim: In reports through ʿAṭāʾ and Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet began reciting before Gabriel finished, eager to retain the revelation and afraid it would slip from memory, so God forbade this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء وأبي صالح: (كان النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- يبادر جبريل فيقرأ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r6.claim: The command means do not recite until Gabriel has completed reciting the revelation to you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r6.anchor: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن} أي: بقراءته {من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r7.speaker: المفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r7.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal interprets the phrase as before the revelation is fully delivered and completed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r7.anchor: وقال المفضل: (من قبل أن يوفى ويتمم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r8.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says the Prophet strained to memorize every revelation before Gabriel departed, fearing he would forget it; this verse was then sent down.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: (كان رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالقرآن أتعب نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r9.claim: The author links the command to 75:16 and notes that al-Kalbī holds this recitation interpretation while al-Farrāʾ and Ibn Qutayba choose it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r9.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r10.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r10.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda understand the command as not reciting a newly revealed verse to anyone until God makes it clear; the author says this bars recitation and dictation before its meaning is clear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وقتادة: (لا تتله على أحد حتى نبينه لك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r11.claim: In ʿAṭiyya's report, Ibn ʿAbbās says not to convey the Qurʾān to people before the explanation of its interpretation comes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r11.anchor: رواية عطية عن ابن عباس قال: (لا تلقه إلى الناس قبل أن يأتيك بيان تأويله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r12.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r12.claim: Some exegetes take the verse to forbid asking for the Qurʾān's revelation before its revelation arrives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r12.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل التفسير أن معنى هذه الآية: (لا تسأل إنزال القرآن من قبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r13.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that a man struck his wife, she sought retaliation, and the Prophet initially ruled for retaliation before this verse came and he paused until 4:34 was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r13.anchor: وروى جرير (¬3) عن الحسن في سبب نزول هذه الآية: (أن رجلا لطم امرأته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r14.claim: The author rejects the claim that the verse was revealed about that incident: the story does not bear on it, apart from its final command to seek increased knowledge; the retaliation ruling was superseded by 4:34.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r14.anchor: ولا تعلق لهذه الآية في القصة التي ذكرها الحسن حتى يقال إنها نازلة فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r15.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r15.claim: God commands the Prophet to ask for more knowledge: teach me what I do not know.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p539/r15.anchor: بأن يسأل الله تعالى زيادة علم، والمعنى: علمني ما لا أعلمه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r1.claim: When Gabriel brought revelation, Muhammad recited along for fear of forgetting; he was told to wait until it was completed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r1.anchor: كان إذا نزل جبريل عليه السلام بالوحي يقرؤه مع جبريل عليه السلام مخافة النسيان، فأنزل الله سبحانه: { ولا تعجل بالقرآن } أي: بقراءته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r2.claim: The instruction means to wait until Gabriel finishes reciting the revelation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r2.anchor: { من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه } من قبل أن يفرغ جبريل مما يريد من التلاوة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r3.claim: Muhammad asks for Qur'anic knowledge; every time a portion came down, his knowledge increased.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r3.anchor: { وقل رب زدني علما } بالقرآن، وكان كلمة نزل عليه شيء من القرآن ازداد به علما.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r1.claim: Taʿālā is from the sense of height: God is exalted.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r1.anchor: قوله: {فتعالى الله} [طه: 114] من باب العلو: ارتفع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r2.claim: Al-Ḥaqq, “the Real,” is one of God’s names.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r2.anchor: {الملك الحق} [طه: 114] والحق اسم من أسماء الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r3.claim: Qatadah explains that the revelation must be clarified to the Prophet before he recites ahead.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r4.claim: Al-Hasan takes the Quran’s completion to include its obligations, limits, rulings, lawful matters, and prohibitions.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: فرائضه، وحدوده، وأحكامه، وحلاله، وحرامه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r5.claim: The Prophet used to recite eagerly during revelation for fear of forgetting, so God told him not to move his tongue hastily and promised to preserve it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r5.anchor: كان النبي عليه السلام إذا نزل عليه الوحي يقرأه ويدئب فيه نفسه مخافة أن ينسى

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r6.claim: He relates the exception to the promise not to forget to 87:6–7 and to God’s power to make His Prophet forget an abrogated verse in 2:106.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r6.anchor: {سنقرئك فلا تنسى {6} إلا ما شاء الله} [الأعلى: 6-7] ، وهو قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] ينسها نبيه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r7.claim: Following the Quran means observing its obligations and limits and acting by it.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says not to hasten until Gabriel has brought the revelation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: {من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} [طه: 114] يعني لا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن ينزل إليك جبريل بالوحي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r9.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r9.claim: Mujahid explains: do not recite it to anyone before God has completed it for you.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p282/r9.anchor:
وقال مجاهد: {ولا تعجل بالقرءان من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه} [طه: 114] ...
لا تتله على أحد حتى نتمه لك.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r2.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r2.claim: Commentators generally explain the admonition through reports that the Prophet feared failing to preserve revelation and hurried to repeat it for memorization.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r2.anchor: Konuya ilişkin rivayetler ışığında 114. âyet genellikle, Hz. Peygamber’in vahyi alırken onu gerektiği gibi koruyamama endişesi taşıdığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r3.speaker: M. Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r3.claim: Asad extends the address beyond Muhammad to Qur’an readers in every age: because the Qur’an is a coherent whole, readers should avoid extracting verses from their general context and drawing hasty conclusions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r3.anchor: M. Esed bu âyetin öncelikle Hz. Muhammed’e hitap etmekle birlikte, bütün çağlarda Kur’an okuyan herkesi ilgilendirdiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r4.claim: The prohibition on haste concerns receiving Qur’anic revelation; the Prophet’s underlying care to safeguard the trust is not condemned.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r4.anchor: Aceleci davranmamasının istenmesi Kur’an’ın vahyi ile ilgilidir; onu bu tutuma sevkeden (emaneti korumada duyarlılık gösterme gibi) âmiller ise kötülenmemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r5.claim: Following the prohibition with a prayer for more knowledge prevents it from sounding like a rebuke, honors the Prophet, and urges him to expand his knowledge and horizons beyond revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r5.anchor: Söz konusu yasak ifadesinin Resûl-i Ekrem’i kınama anlamında alınmaması için bu ifadenin hemen ardından böyle bir buyruğa yer verilerek hem ona iltifat edilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r6.claim: The command encourages efforts to increase knowledge in matters beyond Qur’anic revelation and asks the Prophet to pray to God to broaden his horizons.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:113/r6.anchor: Kur’an vahyi dışındaki hususlarda– bilgisini arttırma çabası içinde olması özendirilmiş, ufkunu açması için de rabbine dua etmesi istenmiştir

BAQILLANI:v1p3/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p3/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p3/r1.claim: The Qur'an is a sufficient, clear proof for God's unity and the Messenger's truth, a guide whose force requires no further proof and whose denial resembles doubting what is directly observed.
BAQILLANI:v1p3/r1.anchor: بين فيه سبحانه أن حجته كافية هادية ولا يحتاج مع وضوحها إلى بينة تعدوها أو حجة تتلوها

BAQILLANI:v1p3/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p3/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p3/r3.claim: Scholars must explain Qur'anic inimitability because it grounds the religion, divine unity, and prophethood, amid widespread ignorance, heresy, and claims that the Qur'an is magic, poetry, or ancient tales.
BAQILLANI:v1p3/r3.anchor: ومن أهم ما يجب على أهل دين الله كشفه وأولى ما يلزم بحثه ما كان لأصل دينهم قواما ولقاعدة توحيدهم عمادا ونظاما

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r1.speaker: السدي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the Prophet strained to memorize each recitation from Gabriel, fearing he would leave before the Prophet learned it; the command not to hasten the Quran was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r1.anchor: عن السدي قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالقرآن أتعب نفسه في حفظه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r2.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti notes another cause had been given in Surat al-Nisa, but prefers al-Suddi’s account as more sound.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r2.anchor: وتقدم في سورة النساء سبب آخر وهذا أصح

NASHR:v2p321/r22.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p321/r22.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p321/r22.claim: Yaqub reads نقضي as an active first-person verb, with accusative وحيه.
NASHR:v2p321/r22.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب (نقضي) بالنون وكسر الضاد وفتح الياء نصبا على تسمية الفاعل (وحيه) بالنصب

NASHR:v2p321/r23.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p321/r23.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p321/r23.claim: The remaining readers use the passive يقضى and nominative وحيه.
NASHR:v2p321/r23.anchor: وقرأ الباقون يقضى بالياء مضمومة وفتح الضاد ورفع وحيه
